families.thesis: A genuine level recovery, with engine choice, availability and effective payments working together. Q3 strength does not establish a further structural growth slope or recovered manufacturer pricing power.
historical_sequence: 2018/19 combined pickups536980/633694; no reliable US LD/Classic/DT allocation. Two-generation breadth and product cycle make peak total an unsuitable LD target.
Pandemic supply stress is background; pre 2024 total pickup decline to468344 in 2022 and444926 in 2023 predates the Hurricane switch. No family-specific pandemic lost-sales allocation established.
2024 LD187013; refreshed1500 launch and upper-trim availability failed to ramp cleanly; Classic wind-down also removed a separate value proposition. Neither explains every lost sale.
2025 LD 204139 (+9.2%); early retail recovery predates returning HEMI deliveries, so HEMI is an additional repair rather than sole cause.
2026 Q1/Q2/Q3 59828/65669/76650; Q3 total +72.8% versus retail +42%. Strong recent pace includes channel effects.
families.customer_mechanism: Customers choose among full-size F-150/Silverado/Sierra/Tundra, used pickups, smaller trucks or delaying replacement. Ram offers cabin/ride/trim choice and restored V8 identity; buyers need not prefer the highest-output engine. Express and Tradesman address entry payments, while missing premium trims previously obstructed different buyers. Warranty limits uncovered repair exposure for eligible first owners but leaves lost time uncovered and does not directly follow the truck into resale. Anecdotes show both Hurricane acceptance and eTorque concerns; no engine-level demand share or failure rate is inferred.
families.dealer_mechanism: Fresh factory-order solicitation with deposits and initially no OEM rebates is evidence at least one dealer seeks future units, beyond clearing old stock. A factory-sold configuration reduces speculative stock/markdown exposure, but no completion or margin is observed. March order-lockable payment support helps convert payment-sensitive buyers and protects them from lead-time offer risk. July clearance support demonstrates stock selling still requires meaningful concessions at that dealer. Dealer-funded discount and OEM rebate are distinct costs. Faster retail turn can reduce holding expense; nationwide profitable voluntary replenishment remains unproved.
counterevidence: Q3 total growth exceeds retail growth; fleet mix or scope can account for part of the increment.
Brand inventory remained elevated in June; not an LD-specific measurement.
Returning HEMI and discounting coexist; neither identifies incremental engine demand.
Fresh-order dealer is a self-described volume specialist, not representative of all franchises.

families.thesis: Hold approximately the current annual level; engineering improvements are relevant, but a persistent post-transition sales gap and selective high-trim clearance do not justify automatic normalization.
historical_sequence: Pre 2024 national HD split unavailable; Canada and Washington proxies cannot allocate US losses.
2024 HD186107 versus 2025 169920(-8.7%). Q1 supplier transition confirms a supply problem, but all four 2025 quarters were below 2024; not just one quarter.
Q12025 HD retail+18% while total-12.7% shows channel/coverage effects.
families.customer_mechanism: Commercial towing/upfit buyers and recreational towing households face different use cases. Diesel torque, smoother gear spacing, cold starts and easier service matter to load-bearing work; a lighter-duty or gasoline truck can have lower acquisition/maintenance expense if capacity is unnecessary. Cummins confirms top-access filters and software servicing changes, but actual shop hours saved and fuel-cost advantage are unmeasured. Ford Super Duty and GM HD compete for the same jobs; brand/service relationships and correct axle/body/payload matter more than peak horsepower alone. Pickup and chassis-cab ratings differ.
families.dealer_mechanism: Dealer reordering depends on exact cab/axle/diesel/upfit orders and fleet scheduling. More predictable order windows can reduce unwanted inventory; a contract-backed unit differs from a speculative premium diesel. July schedule lists orders open and12–14weeks; not filled orders. August21k premium-HD ad warns that high MSRP does not guarantee dealer gross. Invoice, holdback, dealer cash, fleet concessions and completed sale margins are unavailable. Serviceability can strengthen repeat commercial relationships, without proving lower warranty claims.
counterevidence: Q3 decline persists long after initial 2025 changeover.
Supply schedule still has lead time and may be stale; not proof every configuration is freely available.
Large selective discounts do not establish all HD demand weakness.
Warranty is not downtime insurance and first-owner retail terms cannot be applied indiscriminately to fleets.

families.thesis: Defend roughly60 k annual sales; a functional fleet product, not an automatic return to the 2023 peak.
historical_sequence: 2023 81663, then 2024 65869 and 2025 57591. Public work has not identified whether the 2023 peak reflected fleet batch timing, temporary availability or lasting demand; do not assign causality.

families.customer_mechanism: Operators optimize delivered/upfitted price, usable load space, entry effort, route accessibility, downtime and resale. Low loadfloor and wide cargo area can reduce physical work per delivery; large van capacity avoids repeated trips. Ford Transit, Mercedes Sprinter, used vans and smaller vans are relevant by route/upfit, not merely brand. City will fit some lower-volume urban routes better; big ProMaster retains a capacity use case. EV economics depend on depot charging and route duty cycle; no verified fleet saving supports a separate EV volume premium.
families.dealer_mechanism: Commercial dealer should order against route/upfit needs and credible fleet replacement schedules. Factory supply, bodybuilder completion and customer acceptance all affect cash-cycle length. Merchants lists ICE variants andBEV open with12–14week planning leadtimes, supporting orderability but not demand. Aftermarket body/parts availability and workshop uptime support repeat business; none of these imply measured dealer unit margin. Avoid speculative volume merely to fill commercial stock.
counterevidence: 2023 high has not persisted;2026 YTD still lower.
City can replace some smaller large-van purchases.
No transparent contract backlog, retail/fleet split or matched incentive data.
Vehicle warranty repair coverage is not compensation for interrupted routes.

Alternatives includeusedTransitConnect/oldCity, small pickups with caps, minivans, and downsized full-size fleet purchases. At$39995entry this is not a revival of historic low purchase prices.
